sections.title: Situation
sections.prompt: What are the executives really asking, and which numbers frame the answer?
criteria: Derives 2,000 frauds a month and $130k a month per recall point
Shows the recall gap rests on 4 net claims out of 40 (8 disagreements, 6–2)
Explains that a model flagging nothing scores 96% accuracy
States that rollback is ruled out by the privacy rule

sections.title: Stakeholders
sections.prompt: Who is reacting to which number, and how do you bring each along?
criteria: Pre-briefs the SIU director and compliance before Thursday
Gives the CFO the cost per recall point in dollars
Includes the chief claims officer's concern about false alarms on honest claims
Ends with one idea that ties the stakeholders together

sections.title: Options
sections.prompt: What messages could you take into the room, and how does each fare?
criteria: Includes 'accuracy is up' and 'roll back' as options and shows why each fails
Explains in plain words why accuracy and recall moved in opposite directions
Compares options on truth, action and trust on one table

sections.title: Decision and Trade-offs
sections.prompt: What do you do now, and what does it cost?
criteria: Lowers the threshold now and derives the flag volume (2,900 a month) against SIU capacity
Names what is given up, including the false alarms the redacted version had saved
Says which steps are reversible and that the redaction is not
Sets a revisit with measurable triggers after the replay

sections.title: Economics
sections.prompt: How uncertain is the gap, and what does knowing cost?
criteria: Derives a 95% range for each recall figure (e.g. 68–91% and 57–84%)
Gives the range on the gap in dollars a month, not only the $1.3M point estimate
Derives the sample needed for ±5 points (288 frauds) and compares audit cost with the replay
Shows precision and false alarms a month for each version

sections.title: Org and Ownership
sections.prompt: Who owns the threshold, the replay and the fix?
criteria: Names a single accountable owner
Makes the SIU director a co-owner of the threshold
Requires compliance sign-off on each new signal

sections.title: Plan and Milestones
sections.prompt: What happens between now and the fix?
criteria: Lowers the threshold before Thursday
Commits to a narrowed range by a date (two weeks)
Has a measurable gate before the fix ships

sections.title: Risk and Governance
sections.prompt: What could still mislead, and what controls it?
criteria: Names the bias in replaying historical frauds and how to check it
Adds a recall gate to future releases
Retires accuracy as a headline metric

sections.title: Metrics
sections.prompt: How will leaders read model quality from now on?
criteria: Pairs recall with precision or SIU load as a guard
Reports every eval figure as a count out of n with a range
Ties a metric to dollars of leakage

sections.title: Communication
sections.prompt: What exactly do you say on Thursday?
criteria: Gives an opening line that answers 'broken?' and 'roll back?' in plain words
Puts the slide in counts out of 40 and dollars, not jargon
Answers 'is the AI broken?' by explaining fewer flags, not by citing accuracy
Answers 'why not roll back?' with the rule and the fix date
